findings_to_judge.finding: Planet's remaining performance obligations FELL sequentially last quarter - $852.4M at 2026-01-31 to $816.0M at 2026-04-30, a $36.4M decline against $94.2M of revenue recognised, i.e. RPO book-to-bill of roughly 0.6 - and the May-July quarter now being reported contains no announced nine-figure booking at all, only two seven-figure deals (Scottish Government, 30 Jul; a European defence customer PR'd 9:01am today), so a second consecutive sequential RPO decline is likely while the headline still shows a large YoY gain.

Planet's own Q3 FY26 release states the NRO renewed its baseline EOCL contract for PlanetScope broad-area monitoring for $13.2M 'through June 2026' - so Planet's anchor US intelligence contract expired inside the quarter just reported, and no renewal has been announced anywhere in the June-September 2026 window even though Planet press-released two seven-figure European deals in that same window.

findings_to_judge.finding: FY27 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $0-10M against FY26 actual adjusted EBITDA of $15.5M - profitability guided DOWN while revenue is guided up ~41% - and the EBITDA range has stayed $0-10M through two upward revisions to both revenue ($415-440M to $425-441M) and gross margin (50-52% to 52-54%), which arithmetically requires roughly 30% opex growth; Planet's job board currently carries 114 open requisitions, overwhelmingly quota-bearing sales, pre-sales and customer-success roles in Berlin/Netherlands/UK.

The one thing that has historically broken Planet's satellite-services revenue recognition - launch and delivery slippage - did not happen this quarter: three additional Pelicans launched 2026-05-03 and Pelican-11, the Gen-2 technology demonstrator, launched 2026-07-07 on Transporter-17, both inside the 1 May - 31 July window that the $102-107M guide depends on.
